findings.title: ES384 and ES512 tests use a 256-bit EC key and never test >127-byte DER lengths or JCA verification
findings.body: `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` generates a default 256-bit (`secp256r1`) key pair that is reused across `testES256`, `testES384`, and `testES512`. Because the ECDSA signature integers `r` and `s` are bounded by the curve order of the key (32 bytes for P-256) regardless of the hash algorithm, `BigInteger` strips the leading zero padding added in `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` and encodes 32-byte integers in all three tests. Consequently, `testES384` and `testES512` never test 48-byte (`secp384r1`) or 66-byte (`secp521r1`) signature integers, and `testES512` never exercises the multi-byte DER length encoding/decoding path (`length > 127` in `ASN1Encoder.writeLength` and `ASN1Decoder.readLength`, since a real P-521 DER signature sequence is ~136 bytes). In addition, the test only checks that `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` can decode its own output (`Assert.assertArrayEquals(rsConcat, rsConcat2)`), without verifying `asn1Des` against `Signature.verify(asn1Des)` or `sign`.

findings.title: Indefinite length (0x80) and sequence length mismatches are not handled safely in ASN1Decoder
findings.body: `readLength()` returns `-1` when the length byte is `0x80` (BER indefinite-length encoding, which is not valid DER), but none of its callers check for `-1`. In `readInteger()`, passing `length = -1` to `read(length)` throws an unchecked `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of `IOException`. In `readNext()`, `length += reset()` adds the header byte count (typically 2) to `-1`, resulting in `read(1)` which desynchronizes the stream position in `readSequence()`. Furthermore, in `readSequence()`, the loop `while (length > 0)` subtracts `bytes.length` without checking that `length == 0` when finished, so an inner element whose length exceeds the sequence length causes `length` to go negative and silently terminates the loop.

findings.title: Redundant ASN1Encoder allocations and writes in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and discard the resulting `ASN1Encoder` instances before performing the exact same calls on lines 119-120 inside `writeDerSeq(...)`.
